title: AI Stocks Are Selling Off! Buying Opportunity or Warning Sign?
creator: Couch Investor
source_note: Collaboration video (collab_byline: The Motley Fool and Couch Investor), with Rachel from The Motley Fool; summary generated from video captions. Attributed to Couch Investor, whose Collaborations shelf it came from.
summary: Couch Investor and Motley Fool's Rachel dissect the AI sell-off: hot CPI (3.7% YoY), 10y Treasury ~5.3%, and credit stress separating well-capitalised quality names (NVDA, ASML, GOOGL, META, MSFT, AAPL - profitable, FCF-rich) from leveraged neo-clouds. CoreWeave deep dive: 2032 bonds below 80c / ~15% yield, ~$50bn+ obligations, interest >$600m last quarter heading >$900m, backlog >$100bn - risk is timing of revenue recognition vs interest, not demand; Couch sees an Nvidia/asset-buyer backstop and says the thesis has not changed overnight, Rachel says holders must understand the debt role (explicitly not 'sell all your shares'). Oracle: debt toward ~$200bn, CDS +26bp to a record 288bp, 2032 yields 7.24%. Anthropic Q3 revenue ~$16.5bn (+46% QoQ) annualising toward $100bn+ exit ARR, possible IPO this year - 'not good enough' at a mooted $2tn valuation. No explicit stock call from Couch - CRWV and ORCL recorded UNCERTAIN (discussion only).
